instructions.en: Write an independent argumentative essay of 400-700 words on ONE of these questions. (A) Should universities admit students mainly on the basis of a single standardised entrance examination? (B) Should zoos stop keeping large, wide-ranging animals such as elephants and polar bears? Take a clear, qualified position, argue it, and respond to the strongest opposing views. Plan, draft and revise on your own: no frames or phrase banks are provided. Before you ask for feedback, score your draft against the checklist and the focus categories; the gap between your self-assessment and the feedback is part of what this stage trains. Draw on your own knowledge, but do not invent statistics: where a figure would settle a point, say what evidence would be needed.

checklist.en: Claim: my thesis is debatable, precise, and qualified where the evidence demands it.
Reasons and evidence: each reason is supported by specific, relevant evidence or reasoning, and its link to the thesis is explicit.
Counterargument: I state the strongest opposing view in terms its supporters would accept.
Rebuttal: I refute, concede and outweigh, or qualify, and I adjust my claim wherever I concede.
Precision and tone: key terms are defined once and used consistently, my register is formal, each claim is as strong as its support, and I invent no statistics.
Structure and style: every paragraph has one job, the logic is easy to follow, and no sentence wastes words.
Conclusion and self-assessment: my conclusion adds nothing new, and I scored my draft on each focus category before asking for feedback.
